# Libraries hosted in osdlc/osdlc

<!-- Generated by sksizer/dev's scripts/sdlc-mirror/assemble.ts; edit
scripts/sdlc-mirror/templates/hosted/packages-README.md there, not here. -->

Each folder under `packages/<language>/` is one library, published to npm from
this repository. Each library's own README says how to use it. This file covers
what holds for all of them.

## Home and publishing

- Each library lives in `packages/<language>/<name>/`, for example
  `packages/ts/command-seam/`, and is published to npm from this repository.
  Only TypeScript libraries exist today, under `packages/ts/`.
- Each release is tagged `<name>/vX.Y.Z`, for example `tsconfig/v0.3.3`.
  The name keeps one library's tags apart from another's, so it must be
  unique across `packages/*/`. The sdlc CLI's own tags are plain `vX.Y.Z`.
- `.github/workflows/packages-publish.yml` publishes a library when its tag
  is pushed. It uses npm trusted publishing, so no long-lived npm token is
  stored. npm can only set up trusted publishing for a package that already
  exists, so the first version of each library is published once by hand.
  That first publish also leaves a `0.0.0-stage` placeholder version on npm.
  It is harmless and stays.
- A release of a copied library pushes straight to `main`. The admin bypass
  on the `Protect main` ruleset lets it through. The tree is checked before
  the push, and `packages-publish.yml` checks it again before anything
  reaches npm.
- A library can move to its own repository later if it grows.

## Why one repository

One public repository is simpler to secure and maintain than one per library.
The libraries change together: the shared TypeScript and Prettier configs set
the rules for the others. `command-seam` links both through this workspace,
so a config change here runs against its build in CI.

## Where changes are made

Developed here, in this repository:

- `packages/ts/tsconfig` (`@osdlc/tsconfig`)
- `packages/ts/prettier-config` (`@osdlc/prettier-config`)

The development repository takes them from npm, like any other consumer.

Developed in the maintainer's development repository and copied here with
each release:

- `packages/ts/command-seam` (`@osdlc/command-seam`)

A change made to a copied library here is replaced by the next release. Open
an issue or a pull request here, and the maintainer ports accepted changes.

### Releasing a library developed here

1. In a pull request, bump `version` in the library's `package.json` and add a
   dated section to its `CHANGELOG.md`. Merge it when `test` and `verify`
   pass.
2. Tag the merge commit `<name>/vX.Y.Z` and push the tag, for example
   `git tag tsconfig/v0.3.3 <sha>` then `git push origin tsconfig/v0.3.3`.
3. `packages-publish.yml` checks the library and publishes it with
   provenance. If `publish` fails on the npm side, fix the trusted publisher
   setting on npmjs.com and re-run the failed job. Do not re-tag.

## Working on a library

The repository root is a pnpm workspace that holds only `packages/ts/*`.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run build
pnpm run test
```

The root scripts run each library's script of the same name.
